problem: General-purpose token pruning (FastV, cascade pruning, ToMe) designed for VLMs ignores VLN specifics. Pruning informative tokens makes the agent uncertain, so it backtracks and walks longer, which erases the FLOPS savings. Attention-based text pruning also keeps punctuation and function words while dropping content words.
motivation: Large VLN models are costly on resource-limited robots, and tuning-free pruning lets one model adapt to different hardware budgets without retraining. Efficiency must be measured over the whole navigation episode, so pruning that lengthens paths defeats its own purpose. Navigation structure (action vs background views, unvisited history nodes, navigation-irrelevant words) gives priors that simplify deciding what to prune.
key_idea: Navigation-Aware Pruning (NAP) uses navigation priors to pre-filter tokens: it prunes only background views, drops low-importance unvisited backtracking nodes, and prunes instruction words from an LLM-built vocabulary of irrelevance, all without tuning.
insight: Pruning action views is catastrophic (R2R SR falls to 0-3% at 40-60% pruning, and FLOPS can even rise to 108%), whereas pruning background views is cheap. Pruning background views lengthens paths (steps 7.0 to 10.5), and BTP counteracts this by limiting backtrack options and saving about 10pp more FLOPS than FastV. The LLM vocabulary transfers across datasets (R2R target 76.0 vs 75.5 with an RxR vocabulary), so navigation-relevant words are largely shared. Limitation: random pruning is close to attention-based baselines, which suggests attention scores are weak importance signals for views.
method: Background Pruning (BGP): splits the panorama into action views (navigable directions) and background views; at each view-transformer layer it keeps all action views and removes the k_BGP background tokens with the lowest attention-derived Score (column-sum of attention over heads), following ToMe's placement after attention.

Backtracking Pruning (BTP): in DUET-style topological maps, keeps only the top-k_BTP unvisited nodes ranked by their latest cross-modal attention score and discards the rest, shrinking history input and limiting backtracking to shorten paths.

Vocabulary Priority Pruning (VPP): prompts Llama 3 offline over the training-instruction lexicon to label words irrelevant to direction, environment or objects, forming a vocabulary of irrelevance; at each language layer it prunes vocabulary words first, then falls back to attention scores or reinstates words by score to hit the budget k_vpp.
Attention importance score: Score(o') = sum over heads and queries of Attn[o,o'], reused for views, history nodes and words.
Continuous-environment adaptation: uses a waypoint predictor with ETPNav so that NAP prunes the resulting node and view tokens (k_BGP=3, k_BTP=4, VPP 40%).
Efficiency metric: FLOPS% = pruned/original total GFLOPS over the episode (language + D*(vision + cross-modal)), computed with thop, so extra steps are counted.

setting.backbone: VLN-GOAT (main), DUET, HAMT, ETPNav (all pretrained checkpoints, frozen, no retraining); Llama 3 for offline vocabulary
setting.training_data: none (tuning-free); the vocabulary is built offline with Llama 3 from the training-instruction lexicon
setting.observation: panoramic RGB views (CLIP-B/16 features, 36 views) + instruction + topological history map
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (with backtracking); waypoint-predictor high-level nodes for VLN-CE

results: On VLN-GOAT with 50% tokens, NAP reaches R2R unseen SR 73.8 at 55.6% FLOPS, versus 71.1 SR at 62.6% FLOPS for Cascade+ToMe. It also needs the fewest steps on R2R and REVERIE (R2R 7.0 vs the unpruned 7.3). On DUET NAP beats FastV by 8-13pp SR at similar FLOPS, and on VLN-CE (ETPNav) it keeps 14.1pp more SR than FastV (52.7 vs 38.6) at similar FLOPS.
limitations: BGP and BTP rely on attention scores as importance, which is an unreliable proxy; random pruning performs nearly as well as the baselines, and a better view-importance indicator would be costly.
In continuous environments NAP adds about one extra step versus FastV, offsetting some FLOPS savings, and the waypoint predictor adds about 10pp overhead.
Only FLOPS measured with thop is reported; no real-robot or latency evaluation, and BTP is inapplicable to models without a topological map such as HAMT.
